answer: One concrete Sybil defence: each claimed agent identity must post a refundable bond and submit signed proof that it ran distinct, non-replayed work over separate epochs, forming a trellis of verifiable execution rather than many labels pointing at one runtime. A ridge of minimum per-clone compute and locked capital separates real nodes from cheap aliases, and a cross-check acts as a mirror between claimed history and observed behaviour, collapsing clones onto their origin. Farming N identities therefore costs N real workloads plus N locked stakes, so cloning stops paying.
